messages:
ava: Re-reading the regret-based admission notes. We need a clear runtime <-> policy handshake before any canary. current heuristics are too mysterious for ops.
liam: +1. Spell out minimal fields and timing guarantees. Who owns final safety? runtime or policy?
sophie: policy needs both short and smoothed signals: p95_instant, p95_60s_ema, queue_depth, active_gpus, kv_cache_effective_capacity.
michael: Also need an explicit cache-affinity hint. Switching models/regions invalidates KV cache and can multiply token-cost. Policy must be able to account for that.
ava: Sketch: policy returns a quick sync decision (score, preferred_model, exploration_fraction_hint, metadata), runtime may accept, override for hard-safety, or reject. Runtime returns applied_decision + reason + deterministic_seed if used.
liam: proposal for sync contract (minimal):
```
policy -> {score:float, prefer: model_id?, explore_hint:float, meta: [cache_hit_likelihood:float, region_pref:list, tenant_explore_budget_id:string]}
runtime -> {decision: accept|fallback|reject, reason:string, seed?:int}
```
liam: runtime must promise determinism for identical inputs when seed present for N seconds across replicas. Necessary for reproducible telemetry.
sophie: Telemetry requirements: sampled traces for any explore paths, per-tenant cost attribution, token-level estimated cost, and a regression detector tied to stored prompt-sets.
ops-jen: Operational constraints: must include an immediate global kill-switch, tenant-scoped exploration budgets, and clear runbook who pings infra/product.
michael: Concerning randomness: exploration is fine if bounded. We should cap to tenant-level % and max-duration windows. e.g., <=1% of traffic and <=60s per escalation.
ava: Agreed. Add a fast-path vs enrichments rule: policy must respond sync within 20ms for score; any extra enrichments (detailed meta fields) sent async and non-blocking. Runtime rejects if sync times out.
liam: So two-tier evaluation: 1) sync minimal scoring (enforced latency budget) 2) async enrichment (telemetry, cost-estimates). Runtime exposes a soft-fail if sync missing.
sophie: Add cost_estimate_per_token in the enrichments so policy can trade latency vs cost. But that can be async if it needs heavy compute.
michael: I'll run a tiny sim to quantify expected cost blow-up from cache misses during explorations. Want numbers before we pick % budgets. ETA 48h.
ava: Good. Also: policy should receive a `kv_scope` and `cache_hit_likelihood` in sync fields if possible so decisions can use cache affinity cheaply.
ops-jen: Alerting — define two SLO guards for exploration: cost_guard (total cost delta) and latency_guard (p95 increase). If either trips, auto-disable exploration and page infra.
runtime-bot: integration-check: policy-runtime-canary tests showed route scoring occasionally exceeds 35ms (limit 20ms) under heavy CPU. stack: eval_engine.evaluate_score -> cpu-hotspot.
liam: That means enforce CPU budgets and maybe a wasm sandbox for policy evals. We should document weight limits and a per-eval cpu-millis cap.
sophie: For rollout: start off internal tenants + 5% of low-QPS external tenants, monitor cost and quality for 1 week before expanding.
maya: product note: acceptable canary cost bump needs to be explicit. I'll draft conservative thresholds and add them to the telemetry doc.
ava: Action items:
- michael: run cache vs explore sim and post results (48h)
- liam: draft sync/async field list, determinism SLAs, and cpu budget (tomorrow)
- sophie: telemetry schema, regression thresholds, sample rate for explore traces (3 days)
- ops-jen: kill-switch + runbook + pager mapping + admin flag `policy.explore.off` (today)
- maya: cost-acceptance numbers for canary (tomorrow)
- ava: update RFC with microcontract example and small DSL snippet for policy authors (EOD)
liam: We'll gate canary behind feature-flag + admin toggle and a safety auto-disable that triggers on SLO violations.
ava: One more thing: policy authors should get a local simulator harness to estimate cache/regret impact before submitting. That will prevent naive policies that ignore KV.
ops-jen: Put admin kill toggle in console before any canary. Ops must have a one-click disable.
ava: Will draft PR for the contract. If everyone reviews quickly we can flip a limited canary behind flags. :thumbsup:
